skill.name: configuring-tmux
skill.description: Helps configure tmux status bars, plugin frameworks, widgets, and reload workflows with examples for oh-my-tmux, Catppuccin, tmux-powerline, TPM, and tmux 3.2 multiple bars.
skill.summary: Guide tmux framework setup, status bars, plugins, widgets, and troubleshooting.
skill.author: ibrahimhka

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, tmux syntax, expected dotfile paths, and documented public URLs. The fixed /tmp cache examples and pane-content persistence setting are real local privacy and integrity concerns. No prompt injection or data-exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Fixed cache files are placed under /tmp.
remediation.suggestion: Use a user-owned cache directory such as XDG_CACHE_HOME with private permissions and unique filenames.

remediation.issue: tmux-resurrect pane content capture is enabled by default.
remediation.suggestion: Make pane-content capture opt-in and warn users that saved panes can contain secrets.

remediation.issue: Setup commands modify tmux dotfiles and create a symlink.
remediation.suggestion: Ask before changes, back up existing tmux files, and show proposed edits before reload.

remediation.issue: The skill installs third-party tmux plugins and frameworks.
remediation.suggestion: Ask for confirmation before cloning, prefer pinned versions, and advise users to review upstream repositories.

static_findings.snippet: - Theming via `tmux_conf_theme_*` variables in `~/.tmux.conf.local` — never edit `~/.tmux.conf`
- **Gotcha:** its theming layer owns bar 0 and overrides raw `set -g status-right` — use `status-for
- Module list controls bar 0 — add custom `#()` calls via `status-right-append`
tmux 3.2+ supports 2–5 bars. **The correct syntax is `status-format[]` array** — not `status2-right`
Verify: `tmux show-options -g status` (must equal your total bar count)
Scripts in `#()` must emit **one line**. Multi-line output corrupts the bar.
Use `-A "Mozilla/5.0"` — Yahoo blocks default curl UA:
| `set -g status-right` overridden | Use `tmux_conf_theme_status_right=` (oh-my-tmux) or framework e
| New bars not visible | `tmux show-options -g status` must equal bar count |
| Script works in terminal, blank in bar | tmux `#()` has minimal PATH — use `~/` or absolute paths
- Theming via `tmux_conf_theme_*` variables in `~/.tmux.conf.local` — never edit `~/.tmux.conf`
tmux source-file ~/.tmux.conf        # full reload (re-applies framework theming)

content.user_title: Configure tmux Status Bars and Widgets
content.value_statement: tmux status bars can be hard to customize because frameworks override many settings. This skill guides framework choice, plugin setup, widgets, multiple bars, and reload checks.
actual_capabilities: Compare oh-my-tmux, Catppuccin, tmux-powerline, and user-provided frameworks before setup.
Provide TPM plugin configuration for resurrect, continuum, CPU, and network speed modules.
Explain tmux 3.2 status-format array syntax for multiple status bars.
Design status widgets for weather, finance, news tickers, and world clocks.
Troubleshoot missing bar changes, blank widgets, reload problems, and framework overrides.
Show caching patterns for network-backed status widgets.
limitations: It does not verify third-party plugin repositories or their runtime behavior.
It cannot guarantee compatibility with every tmux theme or terminal font.
Network widget examples may need API changes when providers update endpoints.
Dotfile edits should be reviewed before applying them to an existing setup.

use_cases.title: Standardize terminal setup
use_cases.description: Create a consistent tmux framework, plugin list, and status layout for development machines.

use_cases.title: Add workflow widgets
use_cases.description: Add clocks, system metrics, finance data, weather, or news to a daily tmux workspace.

use_cases.title: Resolve framework conflicts
use_cases.description: Diagnose why tmux status changes disappear after reloads or conflict with a theme framework.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up My First Bar
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me configure a simple tmux status bar. Ask which framework I use, then suggest safe beginner settings.

prompt_templates.title: Add Status Widgets
prompt_templates.prompt: Add weather, finance, news, and world clocks to my tmux status bar. Use one-line outputs and caching where needed.

prompt_templates.title: Fix My Bar Config
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my tmux status configuration. Identify why changes are not visible and explain the reload steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Multi-Bar Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a tmux 3.2 setup with three status rows, framework-owned bar zero, custom widgets, and plugin integration. Include safety checks before edits.

output_examples.input: I want a tmux bar with time, CPU, and network speed.
output_examples.output: A framework recommendation, plugin list, widget layout, reload checklist, and notes about font or theme dependencies.

output_examples.input: My second tmux bar is blank.
output: Check the tmux version and row count first.
Confirm that the framework is not overwriting the default bar.
Verify each widget emits one non-empty line.

output_examples.input: Add finance and news widgets to tmux.
output_examples.output: A plan for one-line scripts, cache intervals, provider limits, and fallback text when network requests fail.

best_practices: Ask before changing dotfiles, then back up the current tmux configuration.
Keep network widgets cached and limited to one output line.
Use framework-specific theme variables when a framework owns the default bar.
anti_patterns: Installing plugins from unknown repositories without user approval.
Using fixed shared cache paths for private widget data.
Editing raw status options when the active framework will overwrite them.

faq.question: Does this skill install tmux by itself?
faq.answer: No. It gives setup guidance and commands for tmux configuration after the user chooses a framework.

faq.question: Which tmux frameworks does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers oh-my-tmux, Catppuccin, tmux-powerline, TPM plugins, and user-provided frameworks.

faq.question: Can it create multiple status bars?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains the tmux 3.2 status-format array used for multiple status rows.

faq.question: Does it support network-backed widgets?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows cache patterns for widgets such as finance, weather, and news tickers.

faq.question: Will it edit my existing dotfiles safely?
faq.answer: It instructs the assistant to ask before touching config. Users should still review backups and proposed changes.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
